title: Animations are applied to the wrong object/property
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.stable
- Not reproducible in: 4.5.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9174) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

I have encountered a very strange bug that only occurs when using certain specific node names and property names. Whilst trying to create a minimal repro from my main game project, I simplified and renamed things and noticed that certain renames "fixed" the bug, which I'll detail below. I did manage to create a minimal repro that reliably reproduces on my machine.

The bug, when it reproduces, is catastrophic. Animations are applied to the wrong objects and the wrong properties. The selection of which is deterministic (though it changes when you change the names), and also different between the editor and runtime. I have mostly been testing on discrete properties, but if I switch to floats and continuous interpolation, it gets even weirder as it interpolates to values higher than the highest keyframed value (e.g. I keyframe values variously from 0.0 to 5.0, and I see a node animating from 5.0 to 6.0).

Note that my minimal repro is very specific (making small changes "fixes" the bug) but I encountered this in a large project with dozens of objects and tracks, and in that project many of the characters were exhibiting the wrong animations so it was not just isolated to two specific objects.

**It appears to be a regression in 4.6.**

### Steps to reproduce

**The setup**

I have a scene with two nodes: `Char2` and `Char3`. These both have the same type, and that type has two properties: `ani_1` and `ani_2`. Now, I create an AnimationPlayer and create four tracks: `Char2:ani_1`, `Char2:ani_2`, `Char3:ani_1` and `Char3_ani_2`.

I set up a bunch of keyframes with fully unique values:

* Char2.ani_1 is supposed to go from 0 to 1 (at 1 second).
* Char2.ani_2 is supposed to be constant 2.
* Char3.ani_1 is supposed to go from 3 to 4 (at 2 seconds).
* Char3.ani_2 is supposed to be constant 5.

Note that there is **almost no code** in the project. The only code is just to create a class with the desired attributes:

```gdscript
extends Node

@export var ani_1 : int
@export var ani_2 : int
```

**The bug**

Now select Char2 and play the animation in the editor, observing the changes to the values on the right. Char2.ani_1 takes the animation intended for Char3.ani_2. Char2.ani_2 takes the animation intended for Char3.ani_1. Char3 doesn't get any changes at all (it stays at 0).

I have tried using different types (String, float), using continuous rather than discrete (it gets even weirder), using a RESET track (it doesn't help, simply exhibiting the same behaviour), showing the properties in labels and running the game. None of these fixed the issue.

However, changing the names of the nodes or attributes does usually fix the bug (which is quite concerning - I can use this to "work around" the bug but it feels like there is something very unpredictable going on underneath).

(You might be wondering why I started counting from Char 2?) If I change to Char1 and Char2, the bug goes away.

Also it seems to require a property that starts with "ani" and has an underscore followed by a number. Seriously. Here are all the names I tried:

* animation_1, animation_2: Bad
* anix_1, anix_2: Bad
* ani_1, ani_2: Bad
* bni_1, bni_2: Good
* a_1, a_2: Good
* an_1, an_2: Good
* ani1, ani2: Good
* anima_1, anima_2: Good
* anione, anitwo: Good
* animation_x, animation_y: Good
* animation1, animation2: Good
* prop_1, prop_2: Good
* prop1, prop2: Good

Most property names fixed the issue, but those first three all exhibited the same results. Therefore I have a workaround which is to just use different property names.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Reproduction project for 4.6:
[wrong_animations_repro_4.6.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25259832/wrong_animations_repro_4.6.zip)

Down-converted to 4.5 to demonstrate that it does not manifest in 4.5, as far as I can tell:
[wrong_animations_repro_4.5.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25259840/wrong_animations_repro_4.5.zip)
(Opening the 4.5 project in 4.6 will upgrade the project and it will once again exhibit the bug.)
